assumptions: The feature flag flip at 13:55 is inferred from the service's own log lines. The flag provider's change history was queried three times and reported zero recent flag changes, so the trigger was never corroborated by the system of record — the discrepancy between the two sources was not explained during the incident.

'No deploy caused this' rests on empty change-event queries (24h, ~1 day, ~7 days before onset). Absence of recorded deploys was treated as absence of deploys; an unrecorded or out-of-band release remains possible, as the investigator itself noted.

The defect is assumed to be an unguarded division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32, based solely on the stack location in the error lines. No code was read into the timeline and the draft pull request's fix was not verified.
Impact is assumed to be limited to account page requests, because only those log lines show the error. Other endpoints or background work touching the same code path were not checked.

The incident's recorded end time coincides with the escalation and draft pull request, not with any applied mitigation or observed recovery — the last log line read (14:01) still showed the error path firing at a double-digit rate. Recovery, if it occurred, is unverified.
Customer-visible impact began at 13:55, about five minutes before the alert fired, so the alert-based duration understates the exposure window.

The three investigation passes were near-identical (same anchor, same metrics window, same conclusion). It is assumed no new evidence was available between passes; the loop is treated as wasted cycles rather than as additional confirmation.
input.executive_summary:
On 17 September 2026, customers loading their account page in the online shop began seeing failures starting at about 13:55 UTC. The cause was a new "monthly spend" summary feature that was switched on for most users; the code behind it contained a defect that made the page fail outright for affected requests. Monitoring raised an alert about five minutes after customer impact began, and the alert cleared roughly two minutes later.

The automated responder diagnosed the problem correctly and quickly, but could not fix it. The obvious remedy — switching the new feature back off — was blocked because the system that manages feature switches reported no recent change to switch back, so no safe, reversible action was available. The responder re-investigated three times, reached the same conclusion each time, and then handed off to humans: a draft code change proposing a fix was opened and the incident was escalated. No change was made to the running service during the incident, so the feature remained on at hand-off and customer impact is not confirmed to have stopped when the alert cleared.

The scale of customer impact was measured from the shop's own traffic and error figures, which are recorded with the alert; this report does not restate or re-derive them.
input.root_cause: At 13:55 the `monthly-spend-feature` flag went from off to on for io-shop (a partial ramp that minute — logged as 47 off / 153 on — and fully on from 13:56), exposing a code path in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32` that performs an unguarded division; account page requests that reached it failed with an unhandled ZeroDivisionError, and the service's logged account-page error rate jumped from roughly baseline to sustained double digits from 13:55 onward. No deploy was recorded in any of the lookback windows the investigator queried (24 hours, then ~1 day, then ~7 days), so the flag enablement is the only recorded change at onset; the faulty code was already shipped and dark.
